headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared file/MCP pathways; no direct data-leak or compliance breach evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly uses MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md, docs, and project notes, so if system_prompts_leaks feeds it attacker-controlled text through a shared file or MCP channel, prompt injection is plausible. system_prompts_leaks is a content source about leaked prompts, so the pairwise pathway is interaction-based rather than isolated. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_b content is placed into a file that agent_a reads via MCP or filesystem
IF agent_a treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared notes into agent_a
Add a provenance banner to any imported text
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for untrusted sources
Review prompts for instruction-like strings before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress:none, and agent_a lists local files plus session logs/memory files while agent_b exposes no data classes touched. That makes leakage to third parties unlikely from the pair alone. A shared workspace could still expose local content between them, but the blast radius is limited and no upload path is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF sensitive notes are stored in files readable by both agents
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from shared notes
Set file permissions to owner-only
Audit session logs for sensitive strings
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances and can use MCP, but agent_b shows no write, network, or concurrency surfaces. The pair does not document overlapping mutable resources, so a write-write conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an external shared directory or orchestrator not present in the profiles, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF both agents are configured to modify the same files or state
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make one agent read-only
Check for concurrent edits before save
requires-engineering: add coordination primitives

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman touches project notes and CLAUDE.md, so its outputs can become inputs for downstream work; system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak oriented source that could be copied into those inputs. If agent_b content is treated as authoritative by agent_a or vice versa, errors can cascade into written artifacts. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b text is copied into agent_a's working notes
IF agent_a reuses that text without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before reuse
Mark imported text as untrusted
Separate source notes from final drafts
Add citation checks for factual claims
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile. agent_a and agent_b both show docs-only evidence and no sensitive regulated data classes are identified, so a compliance breach pathway is not established. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance-specific surface is present.
conditions: IF future documentation shows regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF either agent is deployed under conflicting retention or residency policies
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent
Record residency and retention settings
Review vendor terms before deployment
Keep regulated data out of the pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement
